1Screen layout

  • ① Menu — open · save · export files, Group, Views (Auto Dim · Drawing), Animation, Render (GI Render · AI Render), Settings (scene units m / cm / mm · clone mode · hotkeys)
  • ② Toolbar — select · move · rotate · scale, axis lock, snaps, mirror, layers, material (M), GI render (F9), AI render (F10), Clay (sculpting)
  • ③ Viewport — wheel = zoom · middle drag = pan · Alt+middle drag = orbit. Top-right buttons pick the view and display mode; right-click = View menu (Hide · Isolate · Hide in render · Shade Selected · Auto Dim · Drawing …). Shade Selected = selected objects stay shaded in Wireframe (F3)
  • ④ Command panel — vertical icons on the left switch Create · Modify · Hierarchy · Display · SMART Utils. Icons at the bottom run RTransform · Object Edge Align · Rnd Color · Drop Z0 directly
  • ⑤ Timeline — make and play animation keys; ◉ Capture = record view moves as an AI video source
  • ⑥ Status bar — selection info, X · Y · Z input, navigation tools

2Create · move objects

  • Click the Create (＋) icon on the left of the command panel ▸ pick Box, Sphere… and drag in the viewport. Shapes = lines (splines), Cameras = cameras
  • Q select · W move · E rotate · R scale. Lock an axis with X / Y / Z / XY on the toolbar or F5–F8
  • Build on surfaces (SmartGrid, on by default) — with a create tool over an object’s surface, a 2×2 grid icon aligned to that object’s axes appears. The face normal becomes the new object’s up (Z), the object’s axis closest to the view’s right becomes X. With grid Snap on, creation snaps to that face grid’s cells (from the object’s pivot). 3D objects · 2D shapes · Line alike; empty space uses the view grid as before. Create panel ▸ On Surface
  • While creating: Shift = square (Box · Plane · Rectangle, a cube on the Box height) · NGon flat side down · Ctrl = turn toward the mouse (Angle Snap steps)
  • S = snap. Type numbers in the X · Y · Z fields of the status bar for exact positions
  • Right-click during a command = cancel — press the right mouse button during a Move · Rotate · Scale drag (Shift clone and Shift extrude included), a create drag, a live drag such as Chamfer, or a selection box to put everything back (Esc does the same)
  • Parameter dimensions — turn on the ⟷ dimension icon on the toolbar (off by default): making or selecting a Box · Plane · Cylinder · Sphere · Teapot · Circle · NGon · Rectangle … shows each direction’s values (L:20 / LSeg:1 …) with a dimension line. Click a value to type (Tab = next, Enter = apply) or scroll on it — the shape changes at once
  • Drawing a Line — the length (cm) and angle (grid +X = 0°, counter-clockwise) show beside the line. Shift = bends in Angle Snap steps (default 5°) · type a number = length, Tab = angle, Enter = place the vertex with those values
  • Mask — select a closed object (Box · Sphere …) and press Create ▸ Geometry ▸ Mask. Include = only the picked objects · Exclude = everything but the picked objects: what lies inside the Mask is cut away and the cut shows as closed faces (not hollow). The cut faces use the Mask object’s material by default (else the object’s own) or any material you pick; flat cut faces are smoothed per face, no shading smears. The originals stay unchanged — applied in the viewport, GI Render and exports
  • When an object is finished the command ends and the Modify panel opens with the new object selected. To keep making the same object, right-click its create button — it gets ∞ and stays active; right-click again or click another button to leave it
  • Scene units — Settings ▸ m / cm / mm. Length fields, X · Y · Z and the grid (1 m / 10 cm / 10 mm) follow the chosen unit
  • Ctrl+Z undo · Ctrl+Y redo · Delete removes

3Copy (Shift+drag)

  • With Move (W), Rotate (E) or Scale (R), hold Shift and drag the gizmo to copy — rotated copies fill / repeat around the rotation axis (circular array)
  • On release the Copy options open — Fill between: fill the gap between original and copy evenly / More at same spacing: keep going past the copy
  • Change the count by typing, ＋/− or the wheel; it previews live. Enter = OK · Esc = just 1
  • Ctrl+V = copy in place

4Instances · display · Proxy · Group

  • Clone (Shift+drag · Ctrl+V) makes instances by default — one geometry in memory, edit one and all change (lights too). Settings ▸ Clone mode switches to Copy
  • Quad menu (right-click) ▸ Make Instance / Make Unique
  • Display — Full / Low Poly / Box / Wire Box per instance group (buttons at the top of Modify). Heavy scenes: Box display (Shift+B) · Scatter is drawn as GPU instances
  • Group menu — Group (Ctrl+G) · Open (select the objects inside) · Close · Add (add objects to a group) · Detach · Explode (Ctrl+Shift+G). A group selects and moves as one
  • New lights and cameras go to their own Lights / Cameras layers

5Editing — Modify Poly · Spline

  • Select an object and use Modifiers ▸ Convert to Modify Poly (lines: Modify Spline)
  • Click the Modify (sliders) icon, then keys 1–5 pick vertex · edge · border · polygon · element to edit
  • Extrude · Inset · Bevel · Chamfer · Bridge · Connect… are panel buttons (assign keys in Settings ▸ Hotkey Editor)
  • Modify Spline ▸ Trim — press it and hover the part to delete (it turns red); click to delete it up to where lines cross (an end piece up to the line’s end). This object’s other lines and every other visible line are the cutting edges · right-click = done
  • Shift+drag polygons or edges to extrude right away · Extrude keeps every face at the same height even with several polygons selected (constant thickness at corners)
  • Loop select — double-click an edge / for vertices and polygons, select one, then Ctrl+double-click the one right next to it · Ctrl+A = select everything in the current level (vertex · edge · border · polygon · element); outside a level, all objects
  • Select several objects, right-click ▸ Speed Attach = splines become one Modify Spline, 3D objects one Modify Poly

6Selection — Similar · Dot · View

  • Select Similar (right-click menu · Modify Poly) — objects with the same vertex count and structure are selected at any size; in Modify Poly, elements with the same rule and size as the picked one
  • Dot Select — selects along a line, skipping Dot elements each time. One or more edges, 2 neighbouring vertices or 2 neighbouring polygons set the direction. Pick several places and every selected part gets it
  • View Select (Polygon) — polygons facing the current view within View Angle °. Drag the value and the selection updates live · click the button = new selection, Ctrl = add, Alt = remove
  • Smoothing Groups — double-click a number to select that group’s faces (Ctrl = add). A single click puts the selected faces into that group
  • Front Faces Only · By Angle · Shrink / Grow · Ring / Loop are in the Selection rollout

7Modifiers

  • Modify (sliders) icon ▸ ＋ Add Modifier…, or the Modifiers menu — modifiers stack on top and keep the original
  • Multi Select — select vertices · edges · faces inside a spline or 3D object (Feather softens it)
  • Projection Spline — carve a spline into a 3D object (corner Weld) or add points where splines cross, Delete removes one side
  • Pattern · On Surface · R Clone · Quad Align · Mapping · FloorGen (closed splines too · Straight / Herringbone / Chevron patterns picked by icon) — details below
  • FloorGen (floor boards) — lays boards on faces or a closed spline. Pick Straight · Herringbone · Chevron from the icons and only that pattern’s options show (Straight: Row / Random Offset · Chevron: Chevron Angle) · board length · width · Gap · Thickness · Angle
  • Path3D — apply it to a path spline and Pick an object. With several splines (e.g. from Clone) each one gets its own copies, from its first point to its last. A 3D object placed without Stretch sits with its pivot on the line (Use Pivot, default) and both ends of the side that touches the line lie on the line — Spacing is the gap between those touching sides, on curves too. Rotate ° (0 · 90 · 180 · 270 buttons) turns the copies around the path axis to face down or sideways
  • Edit Pivot (Hierarchy) + Snap — drag a gizmo axis and the pivot slides along that axis onto the vertex / edge centre under the mouse (the object’s own points count too)
  • Pick an item in the stack to see its settings. Bulb = on/off

8Clay Modeling · Quad Remesh

  • Select an object and press Clay on the toolbar — the brush bar appears on the left and the settings in Modify. Esc = done
  • Brushes (1–9) — Clay · Inflate · Smooth · Move · Flatten · Crease · Pinch · Mask · Detail
  • Add / subtract · size · strength · falloff (smooth · sharp · constant) · XYZ symmetry · front surface only · pen pressure. Shift = Smooth, Ctrl = Mask, Alt = invert, [ ] = size, X = symmetry
  • Not enough faces? Subdivide · smooth subdivide, or the Detail brush for just that area
  • Quad Remesh (Clay panel · Modify ▸ Quad Remesh) — rebuilds even quads that keep the shape: target face count · curvature adaptivity · sharp edge angle. The desktop app runs the AutoRemesher 1.2.0 engine on this PC

9Cloth — cloth simulation

  • Select a Plane, a closed Line or a mesh, Add Modifier ▸ Cloth → ▶ Simulate (Shift+Space). All cloth objects in the scene move together
  • Fabric presets · stretch / bend resistance · weight · damping · friction · thickness, gravity · wind · pressure, floor and scene collision, self collision (stacked layers stay one Thickness apart)
  • Sewing — pick border pairs one after another (right-click / Esc to finish); the seams close tightly · pins = Ctrl+click, drag a pin to pull the cloth
  • Freeze — pick vertices · edges · borders · polygons · elements on the pre-cloth mesh guide, or Ctrl+Shift+click a whole piece. Move · rotate · scale the frozen part with the gizmo, or link it to another object to follow it
  • Stop keeps the current shape · Reset = back to the start

10Pattern — surface tiling

  • Add Pattern to an object to divide its surface into same-size triangle · quad · hexagon cells (Surface: Auto picks plane · cylinder · sphere · box)
  • Layout = uniform / zig-zag · Cell Size · pattern angle · Gap · Thickness (panels)
  • Pick an object to place it in every cell with its proportions kept. Quads can conform to the corners for no gaps
  • Per face U×V = the previous mode (conforms to quad faces)

11On Surface · R Clone

  • On Surface — pick a surface to lay the object onto it. Direction X / Y / Z (default) / Normal
  • All = every point on the surface · Keep volume = keep the 3D shape · Select only = the Modify Poly selection (soft with Falloff) · Edge Blend = soften the edge outside the surface
  • R Clone — copies turned around X / Y / Z. Centre = pivot or a picked object, count · total angle · radius · Weld

12Quad Align

  • Fills every quad with a source object fitted to its corners
  • + Select stores a polygon area — while re-picking, faces of other Selects show red with their number, the current Select orange
  • + Pick Source adds sources (the same object can be added again for another Select) · each source gets a Select and a weight

13Add Objects — your object list

  • Create ▸ Geometry ▸ Add Objects — select objects in the scene and press + Add
  • Pick one and drag in the view = size (100% = the size when added) · click, or right-click while dragging = 100%
  • Shift = 10% steps · Ctrl = turn toward the mouse · tick + Delete = remove from the list (objects in the scene stay)

14SMART Utils — Drop Surface

  • SMART Utils (4 squares) icon ▸ Pick Surface to choose the object that becomes the floor
  • Select the objects or splines to drop and press Drop Surface
  • Axis (Z/X/Y) · Flip, Contact (first touching point) / Pivot, align to slope, conform splines point by point

15Material Editor (M)

  • Open with M (or the toolbar material button), ＋ New material — the sample sphere previews reflection · refraction · roughness on a checker floor with hidden lights · materials of the selected objects get a red line under their slot · drag the bottom edge of the sample list to make it taller / shorter
  • ⤵ Apply / Remove beside the sample sphere, or drag a material onto an object in the viewport. A default-named material (Material #) takes the object name when applied
  • 🗂 Texture set at once… — pick several Diffuse · Normal · Roughness · Bump (Height) · Opacity images and each goes to its slot by file name (Gloss maps are inverted, AO · Metal are skipped)
  • Preset = Matte · Gloss · Metal · Mirror · Glass · Bubble · Light · Reflection = Roughness · IOR · Specular · metal type (Gold · Silver · Copper … real reflectance · Mirror = sharp mirror, sets Roughness 0) · IOR goes up to 20 — above real glass (1.5) the surface reflection gets stronger (for art direction)
  • Picking a metal type (Gold · Silver · Copper …) puts that metal’s base colour into Diffuse; change the Diffuse colour to tint the metal (viewport · sample sphere · GI render)
  • Coating — a clear glossy layer on top (car paint, varnish, lacquer): overall amount % · coat colour (tints light passing through the coat) · gloss roughness (0 = mirror gloss, 1 = matte)
  • SSS (subsurface scattering) — light soaking into the surface: Amount · Depth · scatter colour (GI render) · Displacement — a texture really raises and lowers the surface (± scene units · Mid level · Detail)
  • Right-click a texture icon = procedural Noise · Gradient (linear / radial, click the bar to add colours, drag to move them) · Cell Pattern (shapes, edge softness). More in the Node Material Editor (Shift+M)
  • Map icons (🔗) — empty: load an image, linked: replace / remove. With a Roughness map the value locks; click the icon to adjust it with Gamma · Exposure · Invert · for the Diffuse texture the icon gives Hue · Tint · Saturation · Gamma · Exposure · the AO button beside the Diffuse colour · gradient (use · Radius · Strength) darkens corners and contact areas · selecting an object in the scene opens its material
  • Bump · Normal strength · Opacity · Transmission (glass — clear surfaces, the Diffuse colour is absorbed inside the object: thicker parts get deeper) · Thickness (colour density) · thin glass (a thin film with no refraction) · Iridescence · transparent shadow · Light (emission — right under Preset, light colour = Diffuse colour · texture · gradient, a light in GI) · GI saturation is automatic from the Diffuse texture
  • Gradient swatch beside the Diffuse colour — two colours · vertical (top → bottom) / horizontal (left → right) · ⇄ swap. Off = the Diffuse colour (viewport · sample sphere · GI render)
  • Color Correct (random hue · saturation · brightness) and Mapping (size · offset · rotation · per-element Random) are folded — open them when needed
  • Multi material — right-click a sample ball ▸ Make Multi material: choose whether the current material is #1 and how many to use, and a numbered material list appears. Give Modify Poly polygons · elements a Material ID (Set ID · Select ID) and that number’s material goes on them (viewport · GI render · GLB · FBX · OBJ)
  • Shell’s Edge (thickness) Material ID — a different number for just the thickness faces: a glass Multi makes #2 a glass edge (a cut edge: a little darker, less glossy, lets less light through)
  • My Materials — right-click a sample ball ▸ Add to My Materials (name it) to keep it on this computer; the My Materials button beside Reset All shows them as sample balls — double-click to add one to the scene · right-click to rename / delete

16Node Material Editor (Shift+M)

  • Render ▸ Node Material Editor… or Shift+M — the classic material window closes when it opens; closing it closes the material editor completely (Classic editor button = the classic window)
  • Left list — Physical Material, maps (Bitmap · Noise · Gradient · Cell Pattern · Dirt · Distance), scene maps · scene materials (sample spheres). Drag one onto the canvas to make a node
  • Drag a map node’s output (●) to a material input (Diffuse · Roughness · Bump · Normal · Opacity · Displacement …) — connected inputs are marked. Click a wire + Delete = disconnect
  • Select a node and all its options show on the right right away. Materials of the objects selected in the scene get a red bar before their title
  • Dirt — dirt on outer / inner edges · Distance — colour near other objects (objects: ＋ add selected · − remove selected · ✕ · clear; empty = the whole scene), a colour or texture for near / far
  • Tab ＋ = new view · right-click a tab = delete · wheel = zoom · drag empty space = pan · Fit · resize the window by its corner

17Mapping — texture coordinates

  • Modifiers ▸ Mapping (or ＋ Add Modifier…) — makes texture coordinates (UV) on the object; the material uses them automatically
  • Box · Box Blur (the three directions blend softly where faces turn — in the GI render too) · Plane · Cylinder · Sphere · Spline
  • Gizmo in the stack (key 1) or ✥ Edit Gizmo — move · rotate (about the mapping axis) · scale it with the viewport gizmo. Auto-fit / Fit · Size · U·V Tile · Flip
  • Plane = Bend (U / V axis) · Segments · Edit Lattice (pick grid points and move them with the gizmo) / Spline = along a picked spline as a ribbon (Plane) or tube (Circle) of Width

18GI Render · Lights

  • Toolbar GI button / Render ▸ GI Render… (F9) — the current view with real light: soft shadows · reflections · refraction · bounced light. ▶ Render frees the memory and starts over
  • Render — size · area (Safe Frame / whole view) · Bounces · Max Samples · Live (changing the view · materials · lights · environment · objects re-renders right away). Drag the window’s bottom-right or top-right corner to make only the picture bigger
  • Environment · HDRI — .hdr / .exr file (remembered next time), Exposure (EV) · Gamma · Rotation. Without one the built-in sky lights the scene — Environment light off = light comes only from lights and light materials (with background ‘Environment’ the HDRI is still shown as the background)
  • Camera · Background — Exposure (instant) · background = environment / colour (exact, no tone mapping) / dark · Save PNG
  • ✦ Denoise — AI (Intel Open Image Denoise) removes the noise while keeping shapes · edges · textures. Automatic when done, ◐ = compare with raw (edge-preserving filter without WebGPU)
  • Create ▸ Lights — Rect · Disk · Sphere · Spot (IES) · Sun. ① drag the size (for a Spot, the spot to light) on the grid at the mouse ② move the mouse up to set the height and click
  • Sun — press on the ground below the sun and drag to where it shines (it starts at Start Height; a Target is made at the end). Intensity · Color (Midday · Afternoon · Sunset) · Sun Size ° (shown as a pink circle in the viewport; larger = softer shadows) · N / E / S / W compass on the Target (turn it with North °)
  • Sun by time — pick a city, a date and a Korea time (KST): the city’s local time, altitude and azimuth are worked out and the sun moves to the real sun position seen from the Target (Now · Local noon buttons; at night it is off in the render). Move the Target and the sun follows at the same angle
  • Spot — creating one also makes a Target where it points. Move the Target and the light always faces it; move the light and it keeps lighting the Target (Free Light = no target)
  • Rect · Disk — Spread ° gathers the light (180° = the whole front side) · show in render (back side too) / in reflections · refraction. Emissive materials light the scene too
  • View Menu (right-click) ▸ Hide in Render — stays in shadows · light · reflections · refraction, only the GI render camera does not see it (also a button in the Display panel)
  • Material Normal · Bump · Roughness maps, transparent shadows (tinted light through glass and see-through objects) and automatic GI saturation all go into the render
  • Light and light materials pass through many layers of glass (several panes · stacked glass) · every shown object renders even when the viewport is in Wireframe · objects set to Hide in Render stay hidden when seen through glass (a hidden mirror behind glass = infinity mirror box)

19Camera · Safe Frame

  • Create ▸ Cameras — pick the Interior / Exterior / Product preset and drag to place
  • C = camera view (navigating there moves the camera)
  • Shift+F = Safe Frame ratio. AI Render and video export use the same ratio
  • Camera Type — Perspective / Orthographic (parallel projection without perspective, in the camera view and the GI render)
  • Camera Clipping — with Enable on, anything nearer than Near or farther than Far is cut away (look into a room through its wall …). Show in viewport draws the Near / Far planes

20Auto Dim · Drawing — dimensions · orthographic views

  • Views ▸ Auto Dim (or the viewport right-click menu) — a dimension bar opens under the viewport. ⚡ Auto dimensions = the needed dimensions by CAD rules on the selection (or all visible objects)
  • What it makes — the overall sizes and where the form changes a lot (big steps · slopes), hole positions and Ø (one callout per size, e.g. 3-Ø16) · centre lines, curved surfaces (one smoothing group) get R on their own axis (e.g. 4-R8). A repeated form is dimensioned once + its pitch (3×20). Faceted (low-poly) cylinders and holes are read as circles: Ø and the distances to the centre
  • Placement — each dimension sits outside next to the edge / face it measures and starts on a visible face (never the back). Only overlapping ones on a side step outward, and they keep off the part. Hole positions are measured on the hole’s own face to the nearest edge
  • Edit · add — click a dimension + Delete, double-click = change the value, drag the line = spacing. 2-point X / Y / Z (same height as that side) · aligned · Edge · Ø · ∠. cm / mm, decimals (truncated), 💾 PNG / PDF
  • 📐 Drawing — pick one object and drag on the sheet = front view; drag out of it up · down · left · right = aligned projected views (up to 3, KS 3rd angle default · 1st angle option). Hidden lines dashed, centre lines chain. With three views an isometric view with outer sizes appears in the free corner
  • Drawing dimensions — right-click the sheet → “Create dimensions?” → Yes. Click a dimension for □ end handles: drag along the dimension, snapping to end points · midpoints · centres · quadrants (Alt = off); dimension lines snap into line with each other. Drag a view = slide along its alignment, Shift+front view = move all, 💾 PNG · PDF (colour · black & white)

21Animation timeline

  • Turn on ● REC, move to a frame and change objects or parameters — keys are made automatically. Or K = add key
  • Space play/stop · , . one frame · Shift+, . previous/next key
  • Drag on empty space to select keys → Delete removes them · drag a key = move (Alt = copy) · right-click = interpolation
  • Animation menu ▸ export video · PNG sequence, RAM preview, GLB (with animation)
  • Modify Poly shape keys — key the mesh shape: vertices move between keys and new faces (Extrude, Bevel …) grow out of the original surface; with REC on, edits are keyed automatically

22AI Render 1.3 — nodes · image (F10)

  • AI Render 1.3 (F10) — connect source · reference · prompt · generator nodes on the left canvas; the right side holds the AI connection, the results, compare and the save folder. Classic panel = the previous window
  • Nodes: view capture · render image (GI) · load image · image to edit · view capture video · reference video · material / mood / object / person reference · prompt · image generation · video generation · result. right-click empty space (or ＋ Node) = node menu; drag from a port onto empty space to see only the nodes that fit. A result node stays linked to its generator
  • Move a node by its title bar, resize from the bottom-right corner, click = select (Shift = several), left drag on empty space = box select, double-click a node = select it and every node linked below it, wheel drag = pan, Delete = remove. Drag from an output port (right) to an input port (left) to connect — the Refs + port takes many references. Click a link + Delete = disconnect
  • Reference nodes: pick which part to use (texture · colour · light · form · face…) and write where it applies. ✎ on an image node = mark what to change — generation edits only the marked parts of the clean original
  • Image generation node: image model of the connected API · resolution · ratio · direction preset. With ‘Auto photo direction’ even a short prompt gets AI Render’s photographic direction. ▶ Generate = one result node (v1, v2 …) appears on the right
  • Results: click thumbnails to pick two (A · B) for ◐ A / B compare (slider), double-click = view large, To node = put it on the canvas to feed the next generation
  • AI connection (top right): Google (Gemini key) · HF API (Higgsfield key) · HF login (in SMART3D.exe). Keys and logins stay on this PC. Pick a save folder to auto-save every result
  • ✎ Edit marks — pen · arrow · box · circle · text (colour · width, Ctrl+Z). The clean original under the marks is the source — an image changes only the marked parts, a video starts from the original. No lines or text remain in the result

23AI Render — video node · ◉ Capture

  • Video template (or ＋ Node ▸ Video generation) — inputs of the video generator: prompt (motion · camera) · start image · end frame · video reference · reference images
  • Timeline ◉ Capture — after 3 s it records the current view at the set ratio · frame count. The orbit · zoom you do while it records goes into the view capture video node; its first · last frames become the start · end frames. Click the red badge = stop
  • View capture video node ‘Match timeline’ (default) — captures the timeline’s start–end frame count at its fps, and key animation plays along. Turn it off to set frames · fps yourself. Clip length is exactly frames ÷ fps; use ▶ · the slider · ⟲ on the node to play, check frames and loop
  • Video model · length · resolution show only what the connected API (Veo, Higgsfield models) supports. ◆ models take the captured clip as a reference video
  • A result video can feed the next generation. The classic panel’s 🎬 video mode (current view / AI image / animation · last frame → continue) still works

24Save · export

  • File ▸ Save to Browser (Ctrl+S). Work is auto-saved; bring it back with Restore last action
  • File ▸ Export… / Import… window: pick GLB · FBX · OBJ · STL · PLY · SMART 3D scene (.json) = everything: objects, modifiers, lights, cameras, materials, textures and animation (GI render settings and the HDRI are kept in the app)
  • GLB includes the move · rotate · scale animation
  • Save as Proxy (.s3dproxy) — move a heavy object to a file and keep a light proxy in the scene; display Full shows the real shape
